newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Clinton departs Australia for Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Clinton departs Australia for Philippines.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary left Australia on Saturday boundfor the Philippines and the second leg of their 12-day Asian trip.

The Clintons' five-day Australian visit was a working holiday, aimed at recharging their batteries after the recent gruelling re-election campaign and ahead of a series of Asian bilateral meetings and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit next week.

While Clinton held talks with Australian Prime Minister John Howard and addressed the Australian parliament, the highlights of the visit were golfing with world number one Greg Norman, cuddling a koala and snorkelling on the Great Barrier Reef.
Australia and the United States are long-standing allies, whose relationship periodically encounters hiccups over agricultural trade subsidies.
But on this trip, Clinton reassured Canberra that U.S. agricultural subsidies would not harm Australia, directly or indirectly.
He also bolstered Australia's efforts to integrate with the booming Asian economies, by confirming a shared U.S.-Australia future in the region through stronger defence ties and trade.
